subject: Final alignment: sandboxed prompt pack delivery, usage ledger & takedown cadence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Cora James <cora.james@velotech.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final alignment: sandboxed prompt pack delivery, usage ledger & takedown cadence

Cora —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, I wanted to put the proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and delivery steps in writing so Velotech and Redwood can align on the exchange, acceptance criteria, and takedown cadence for the prompt pack and associated testcases. This is intentionally narrow and sandboxed — purpose: evaluation only.

Summary (high level)
- Deliverable: Prompt pack + sample testcases (ephemeral access)
- Delivery mechanism: S3-fed ephemeral sandbox in us-west2 (Redwood-managed sandbox)
- Licensing: evaluation-only; no redistribution; no model training on full dataset; derived metrics allowed
- Acceptance window: 7 business days after delivery for Velotech to run acceptance testcases
- Takedown: Redwood will revoke access 90 days after provisioning unless both parties agree to extension

Proposed MAP milestones
1) 2026-10-04: Redwood delivers prompt pack (velotech_promptpack_v1.zip) + manifest + MAP worksheet (attached)
2) 2026-10-04 — 2026-10-11: Velotech runs acceptance suite against provided testcases; share runbook results and any failing cases
3) 2026-10-14: Close milestone — acceptance or escalate with remediation plan; if accepted, an optional extended sandbox can be discussed

Operational & security notes
- Access: access is ephemeral and logged; we will provide token-level audit logs for all inference calls tied to Velotech's eval project ID
- Data handling: prompt pack is encrypted at rest; Redwood will not retain copies beyond the agreed 90-day window without written consent
- Allowed usage: evaluation & internal error analysis only; no benchmarking publications without mutual consent

Attachments included for initial handoff: velotech_promptpack_v1.zip (prompt examples + instructions), MAP_Velotech_20261001.xlsx (milestones + acceptance criteria), testcase_manifest_20261001.csv (short manifest)

Ask: Please confirm these milestones and the licensing constraints. If legal needs to propose redlines, loop them into this thread — we can typically turn straightforward evaluation redlines around in 48–72 hours.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: velotech_promptpack_v1.zip (zip - 24MB), MAP_Velotech_20261001.xlsx (xlsx - 120KB), testcase_manifest_20261001.csv (csv - 8KB)

From: Cora James <cora.james@velotech.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final alignment: sandboxed prompt pack delivery, usage ledger & takedown cadence

Kimberly —

Appreciate the write-up and proposed MAP. A few clarifying questions from our side (legal + product):

1) Allowed inferences: can our team run the prompt pack against held-out internal models for comparative analysis, or is this strictly the API surface you host?
2) Token / telemetry: we need clarity on what telemetry you retain (prompt text vs. hashed metadata) and retention windows for logs beyond the 90 days
3) Redlines: our legal team has two small redlines around the takedown clause (data destruction certification) and a short warranty clause — I can have Ben (legal) send the redline doc this afternoon

Operationally we prefer a 14-day acceptance window, but are OK testing in 7 business days if we can get the manifest + sample runbook immediately. Also, can you confirm the sandbox will allow us to pull per-request latency and token counts?

If you can attach the MAP worksheet and the runbook sample, I’ll circulate internally and get back with a sign/mark-up by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Cora James
Head of Research Partnerships
Velotech
cora.james@velotech.ai
+1 (617) 555-0123

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Cora James <cora.james@velotech.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final alignment: sandboxed prompt pack delivery, usage ledger & takedown cadence

Cora —

Thanks — quick responses inline below and I attached the runbook sample (redwood_ephemeral-sandbox-instructions.pdf) and a slightly annotated MAP workbook.

> 1) Allowed inferences: can our team run the prompt pack against held-out internal models for comparative analysis, or is this strictly the API surface you host?
We can support two paths: (A) Redwood-hosted ephemeral inference (recommended for auditability) or (B) a controlled outbound fetch where Velotech runs against an internal stack but only after an approved MTA addendum. For speed, we usually start with Redwood-hosted evaluations so we can provide token-level telemetry and a canonical audit log. If you want (B) we can route through a short MTA addendum — Priyom can coordinate.

> 2) Token / telemetry: we need clarity on what telemetry you retain (prompt text vs. hashed metadata) and retention windows for logs beyond the 90 days
Telemetry: by default we retain token counts, latency, and hashed input metadata for 180 days; full prompt text is logged only when requested for debugging (and then only with a retention TTL we agree on). We will add a certification item to the MAP workbook so this is explicit.

> 3) Redlines: our legal team has two small redlines around the takedown clause (data destruction certification) and a short warranty clause — I can have Ben (legal) send the redline doc this afternoon
Perfect — Ben can send the redline and I’ll route to our contracts manager for a quick review. For straightforward redlines we target a 48-hour turnaround.

Proposed adjusted timeline (single-source in the workbook)
- 2026-10-04: Delivery (prompt pack + manifest + runbook)
- 2026-10-04 — 2026-10-11: Acceptance testing (7 business days)
- 2026-10-14: Close / acceptance or documented remediation plan

If your legal prefers a 14-day window we can extend to 10 business days (closing 2026-10-18) as a compromise — let me know.

Priyom — I’ve cc’d you to coordinate the MTA addendum if Velotech wants an outbound evaluation path. Rishi — FYI for audit log extraction after the run.

Best,
Kimberly

Attachments: redwood_ephemeral-sandbox-instructions.pdf (pdf - 85KB), MAP_Velotech_20261001.xlsx (xlsx - 124KB), testcase_manifest_20261001.csv (csv - 8KB)

Kimberly / team —

We reviewed the MAP and the attached documents. We made two very small redlines (takedown certification language and an explicit return/destruction clause). I’ve applied the redlines to the MAP workbook and initialed the worksheet.

Velotech confirms the following:
- We accept the sandboxed delivery model (Redwood-hosted) and will complete acceptance testing in the agreed window (7 business days)
- We request token-level telemetry and per-request latency metrics during the acceptance window; Redwood confirmed availability
- We agree to the 90-day ephemeral access and will coordinate with you if we request an extension after acceptance

Please find the signed MAP (DocuSign) link below — we’ve signed the MAP with the minor redlines Ben attached. Once you confirm receipt we’ll schedule Redwood’s provisioning to begin on 2026-10-04.
